question: On the homogeneous rolling X_U>0 branch after elliptic-compensator projection, does the neutral fixed RTK scalar change the lapse-stability cross-block entry {pi_N,H_perp} at k=0?

domain.scalar: rolling Sigma(t), X_U>0, no spatial Sigma gradient

target_identities: For homogeneous shift-symmetric P(X_U), p_Sigma=sqrt(g) P_X Theta depends on Theta but not separately on N.
After solving Theta=Theta(p_Sigma,g), H_Sigma=N [p_Sigma Theta-sqrt(g)P(Theta^2/2)] is exactly affine in N.
Therefore H_perp^Sigma=dH_Sigma/dN at fixed canonical variables is N-independent and {pi_N,H_perp^Sigma}=0.
The fixed mixed operator C(X_U) D_iTheta D^iTheta vanishes identically on the homogeneous k=0 support and gives no homogeneous lapse-stability correction.
Hence delta_a_RTK(k=0)=0 in the cross-block support theorem.

decision_rule.if_all_hold: classify the homogeneous neutral-RTK lapse-rank correction as exactly zero; combine only with the separately certified k0 ordinary-matter inheritance theorem, without claiming finite-k rank
decision_rule.if_any_fail: do not inherit the pure-gravity k0 cross-block; derive the nonzero correction explicitly

non_claims: does not prove the pure-gravity homogeneous cross-block is nonzero under every global zero-mode boundary condition
does not prove finite-k rank where D_iTheta and metric dependence of L^{-1} are active
does not certify production cosmological perturbations of the elliptic completion
next_gate_if_pass: freeze a current-lineage homogeneous bridge closure record and then attack the finite-k reduced Pfaffian with resolvent metric variation retained
